We landed on Enoshima under cover of darkness.
As we had yesterday, but far more efficiently. Shortly after midnight, we were already investigating.

We walked as though pushing aside a curtain of night. Perhaps it was the memory of yesterday: the blackness submerging the landscape seemed still more sinister, still more secretive.

Without my noticing, my steps grew heavy. Cautious.

en.html:
The 'Fisheries Research Institute' supposedly stood a little west of the island's center.
At least, that was what the shogunate map said.

If the map did not reflect reality, we would have to locate it ourselves. Hence my preference for securing a place where some clue certainly remained. There was no telling how it might help.

Time, however, was finite. And invariably insufficient.
A detour required haste. I admonished my feet, which were straying from caution into cowardice, and quickened my pace—just short of making noise.

The 'Fisheries Research Institute' supposedly stood a little west of the island's center.
At least, that was what the shogunate map said.

en.html:
I had to fight.
At least until they could escape.

This opponent—
Something I had never faced, nor even imagined facing.
This enemy.
